documents.title: Changes to account fees
documents.text:
To: All Account Holders
From: Greystone Bank
Date: July 15

Dear customer,
Beginning September 1, Greystone Bank will make several changes to its personal checking accounts. The monthly maintenance fee will increase from $8 to $10, but it will be waived for customers who keep a minimum balance of $1,500 or set up direct deposit of at least $500 per month. Withdrawals from other banks' ATMs will cost $2.50 each, up from $2. Mobile check deposit will remain free. Full details are available in the enclosed brochure or at any branch. To change to an account without monthly fees, visit greystonebank.example/accounts.
We value your business.

documents.title: Lakeview Lodge: Booking Policies
documents.text: Check-in is from 3 p.m.; check-out is by 11 a.m. Early check-in may be arranged for $20 if a room is ready. Cancellations made at least 72 hours before arrival are free of charge. documents.title: Westfield Schools to Provide Tablets
documents.text: WESTFIELD (August 22) - Starting this fall, every student in grades 6 through 8 in the Westfield School District will receive a tablet computer for use in class and at home. [A] The district purchased 2,400 devices with a $1.1 million grant from the state education fund. [B] Superintendent Linda Marsh said the tablets will give students access to digital textbooks and reduce the weight of the backpacks they carry daily. [C] Teachers will attend a training session on September 3 to learn how to integrate the devices into their lessons. [D] Some parents have questioned whether the screens will distract students, and the district has said it will install software that blocks games and social media during school hours. Students will be asked to return the tablets at the end of eighth grade.

documents.title: Fire safety inspection
documents.text:
TO: Warehouse staff
FROM: Ivan Petrov, Safety Officer
DATE: April 2
SUBJECT: Fire safety inspection

A fire safety inspection of the warehouse will take place on Thursday, April 11. Inspectors will check extinguishers, emergency exits, and the sprinkler system, and will observe an evacuation drill at 10:30 a.m. All aisles and exits must be clear of boxes and pallets by Wednesday evening. Employees who work the night shift will receive a briefing from me at 5 p.m. on April 9 in the break room. Staff who have not completed the online fire-safety course must do so by April 8; certificates should be sent to my e-mail. Failure to comply with these rules may result in a written warning.

documents.title: A hidden gem
documents.text:
Saffron Table: 5 stars out of 5
Posted by Lena K., November 9

I almost walked past Saffron Table because it is tucked behind a hardware store, but I'm glad I didn't. The menu is small and changes weekly, which suggests that the chef uses whatever is freshest. I ordered the lamb with apricots, which was tender and perfectly seasoned. My dining companion, who rarely likes fish, loved the grilled sea bass. Service was attentive without being intrusive, and the staff patiently explained every dish. The only drawback is that reservations are essential; we were told that weekend tables are booked two weeks ahead. Prices are fair for the quality: $24 to $34 for main courses. I'll definitely be back.

documents.title: Road Construction on Market Street
documents.text: From May 6 to June 28, Market Street between 2nd Avenue and 5th Avenue will be partly closed for the installation of new drainage pipes. Traffic will be reduced to one lane in each direction, and on-street parking will be unavailable. Sidewalks will remain open, but pedestrians should expect noise and dust. Work will take place Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. Delivery vehicles may use the rear lane behind the buildings. Updates are available at citypublicworks.example or by calling 555-0150.

documents.title: Concerns about the construction
documents.text:
Dear City Public Works Department,
I own Bellini Bakery at 340 Market Street. I understand the work is necessary, but eight weeks of construction will seriously affect my business. Most of my customers arrive by car in the morning, and without parking they will go elsewhere. Could you provide temporary signs directing customers to the parking lot behind the library? Also, I would like to know whether businesses can apply for compensation. In the meantime, I plan to introduce a free delivery service for orders over $20.
Sincerely,
Giulia Bellini

documents.title: Museum Unveils Ancient Coin Exhibit
documents.text: HAVERFORD (March 5) - The Haverford Museum of History opens a major exhibition of ancient coins on March 15. "Gold and Silver: Money in the Ancient World" features more than 300 coins on loan from museums in six countries, including rare pieces from Rome, Greece, and Persia. The exhibit, curated by historian Dr. Naomi Feld, took three years to organize. Visitors can handle replica coins in an interactive zone and use a free mobile app to hear audio commentary. The exhibition runs through August 31.

documents.title: Haverford Museum: Plan Your Visit
documents.text:
Hours: Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.; Thursdays until 9 p.m.
General admission: $12. The "Gold and Silver" exhibit requires a special ticket of $18, which includes general admission. Students and seniors pay $9 (exhibit: $14). Tickets can be purchased online; timed entry is required for the exhibit. Large bags must be left in the free cloakroom. Photography is allowed without flash. School groups: call 555-0120 at least 3 weeks ahead.
